record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: Develop superposition theorems for integral input-to-state stability in infinite-dimensional systems that play the role for iISS that Theorem 2.7 plays for ISS. In particular, find non-Lyapunov characterizations of infinite-dimensional iISS comparable to the known finite-dimensional ODE theory.

evidence.quote: • Superposition theorems (counterparts of Theorem 2.7) are not available (for ODEs see [4, 207]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider an abstract control system $\Sigma=(X,\mathcal{U},\phi)$, where:
- $X$ is a Banach space (the state space) with norm $\|\cdot\|_X$ and zero element $0$;
- $\mathcal{U}$ is a normed vector space of admissible input functions $u:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\to U$ (where $U$ is a Banach space of input values), closed under concatenation and time-shifts;
- $\phi:D_\phi\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\times X\times\mathcal{U}\to X$ is a transition map satisfying the standard cocycle/causality axioms (identity, causality, cocycle property, continuity in time on its maximal interval of existence).

Comparison function classes. $\mathcal{K}$ denotes continuous strictly increasing functions $\alpha:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ with $\alpha(0)=0$; $\mathcal{K}_\infty\subset\mathcal{K}$ are unbounded; $\mathcal{L}$ denotes continuous decreasing functions tending to $0$; $\mathcal{KL}=\{\beta:\beta(\cdot,t)\in\mathcal{K},\,\beta(r,\cdot)\in\mathcal{L}\}$.

Definition (iISS). $\Sigma$ is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if it is forward complete and there exist $\beta\in\mathcal{KL}$ and $\alpha,\gamma\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for every $x\in X$, every $u\in\mathcal{U}$, and every $t\geq 0$,
$$\alpha(\|\phi(t,x,u)\|_X)\;\leq\;\beta(\|x\|_X,t)\;+\;\int_0^t \gamma(\|u(s)\|_U)\,ds.$$

Background fact (ISS superposition theorem). For $\Sigma$ as above, input-to-state stability (ISS) is known to be equivalent to the conjunction of two strictly weaker properties: uniform local stability together with a suitable asymptotic gain / limit property (e.g., the bounded-input/uniform-limit property or the ULIM property), generalizing the Sontag–Wang superposition theorem from finite-dimensional ODEs to Banach-space systems. For finite-dimensional ODE systems, an analogous superposition-type non-Lyapunov characterization of iISS is known: iISS is equivalent to forward completeness combined with the global asymptotic stability of the zero-input system and a bounded-energy/converging-input bounded-state property.

Problem. Establish a superposition-type theorem for iISS in the infinite-dimensional setting. Specifically, identify a finite list of qualitative trajectory-based properties $(P_1),\dots,(P_k)$ — none of which involves the construction of a Lyapunov function — such that for every abstract control system $\Sigma=(X,\mathcal{U},\phi)$ on a Banach space $X$,
$$\Sigma\text{ is iISS}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (P_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge (P_k).$$
The characterization should reduce, in the special case $X=\mathbb{R}^n$ with ordinary differential equation dynamics, to the known finite-dimensional non-Lyapunov characterization of iISS, and should play the role for iISS that the ISS superposition theorem plays for ISS.
artifact.status_search_result: Superposition theorems for ISS and, more recently, for input-to-output stability (IOS) of infinite-dimensional systems have been established, and iISS has been characterized in various restricted settings (e.g., 1-D parabolic PDEs, time-varying systems, bilinear systems). However, a general non-Lyapunov superposition-style characterization of iISS for abstract control systems on Banach spaces, analogous to the ISS superposition theorem and matching the finite-dimensional ODE iISS theory, does not appear in the literature; recent surveys (2024) still discuss iISS characterizations as an active and partially developed research direction. Status appears open.

status_evidence.title: Input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional systems: Foundations and present-day developments
status_evidence.snippet: Review of main results on ISS for infinite-dimensional systems, including ISS superposition theorem and Lyapunov characterizations; iISS characterizations discussed as ongoing developments.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2024, no general iISS superposition theorem analogous to the ISS one is reported for infinite-dimensional systems.

status_evidence.title: Superposition theorems for input-to-output stability of infinite dimensional systems
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes IOS superposition theorems containing the ISS superposition theorem as a special case.
status_evidence.claim: Recent superposition theorems target ISS/IOS, not iISS, indicating the iISS case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Input-to-State Stability of Infinite-Dimensional Systems: Recent Results and Open Questions
status_evidence.snippet: Lists as an open question that superposition theorems (counterparts of the ISS superposition theorem) are not available for iISS in infinite dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as open in this survey.
